newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bankruptcies reach record for Menem era.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bankruptcies reach record for Menem era.

text.p: Bankruptcy proceedings in Argentina in 1996 reached their highest level since President Carlos Menem launched his economic and monetary reforms in 1991, Argentine newspapers reported Tuesday.
Data for Buenos Aires showed 2,819 bankruptcy petitions, compared to 2,062 cases in 1995 and just 1,058 for the whole of the 1991-94 economic boom period.
The total number of bankruptcies accepted by the court was 1,755, double last year's total. The firms involved had total debts of $103 million versus $69 million in 1995.
There were 1,100 Chapter 11-type reorganization proceedings, a similar number to 1995.
However for December of this year, there were only 157 bankruptcy petitions -- the lowest in the last 14 months.
